newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends strong after rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends strong after rate hike.

text.p: The Philippine peso erased its earlier losses in a jittery market on Friday after the Central Bank announced at midday it was raising its key overnight rate to 15 percent from 12.75 percent.

The peso ended at 26.372 to the dollar after being pounded to 26.382 as fears were renewed the peso may be hit again by the weakness of the Thai baht. Volume was heavy at $529.5 million compared with $298 million the previous day.
Thailand's woes had forced the Central Bank to reverse its 0.25 percentage-point rate cut in its overnight rate early on Thursday.
The resignation of Thai finance minister Amnuay Virawan caused pressure again on the Thai baht. Just last month, the peso and other Asian currencies were hurt by Thailand's financial problems.
Prior to the increase in its rate, the Central Bank sold as much as $219 million at the rates of 26.379 up to 26.381, traders said.
"The increase in rate is just temporary. It's just to dissuade or discourage speculators," a banker said.
The peso will take its cue on Friday from the spillover effect of the Thailand's problems, traders said.
